**Finding submitted: deviation (§ 14.2.2, p0755).**

- **What fails:** PB's "At-Will Termination" right is gated on SFJ having funded $60 million of Development Costs and expires at first Regulatory Approval — so for the early years of this multi-year program PB has no convenience exit at all. When available, it costs 300% of all Development Costs funded, plus continuing Approval Payments. Both terms fail the fallback (60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee capped near 3 months' fees).
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** convenience termination at any time on thirty (30) days' written notice, and the 300% multiple reduced to 100% of Development Costs actually paid or incurred by SFJ. Level marked *fallback* on the fee because SFJ is funding development, so a zero-payment exit would be disproportionate to the bargain.
- **Noted, not flagged:** SFJ's exits (§§ 14.2.3 Material Adverse Event, 14.2.6 change of control, 14.2.10 JSC disagreement) are "sole discretion" but event-triggered rather than true convenience rights, so they are not separate T4C deviations; a 90-day notice overlay on §§ 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 is a secondary ask if the section is reopened.
